title: Heterogeneous handoff procedure + TF implementation notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic, safety-first approach for performing a phased re-host / handoff of runtime capacity across heterogeneous private deployments (mixed GPU generations, different OS images, and hybrid VPC/on-prem topologies). It mixes operational runbook steps with concrete Terraform module guidance and compatibility checks for control-plane and API layers.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Planned redeploys of runtime nodes and runtime-sidecar proxies across private clusters.
- Terraform implementation patterns for resource replacement with minimal state churn.
- Controls for API compatibility between control plane and runtime shards during traffic migration.
- Rollback and backout strategies focused on state and networking safety.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customer-managed VPCs with peering or Transit Gateway are in use; some sites are air-gapped (no direct internet egress).
- Terraform is the primary infra-as-code tool; state backend is remote (S3/GCS) with state locking via DynamoDB/Storage locks.
- Runtime supports multiple protocol-compatible variants (e.g., fast-quantized vs full-fp) that can be used as fallbacks.
- We can schedule brief traffic steering windows (minutes) but want max 2x transient latency.

High-level strategy summary:
1) Prepare a shadow fleet (new nodes + sidecars) configured by new TF modules but attached to the same control-plane version.
2) Warm up caches and pre-load model artifacts via a staging-only routing policy.
3) Canary small percent of traffic through proxy routing rules with realtime SLO/trace checks.
4) Gradually scale canary while monitoring token-level latency and error trends.
5) Switch routing when metric thresholds are stable; keep shadow fleet ready for immediate rollback.

Pre-upgrade checks (must pass):
- Terraform state: no pending manual locks, plan runs clean in CI (terraform plan exit 0).
- Backups: control-plane DB snapshot taken and stored off-host (tagged with change-id).
- Observability: dashboards for tokens/sec, p95/p99 token latency, model-load times, and tail errors exist and are green baseline.
- Network: BGP/peering routes validated and MTU consistent across nodes.
- Inventory: list of machines with GPU type, driver version, kernel version; match runtime kernel support matrix.

Terraform module notes (patterns & pitfalls):
- Use resource replacement patterns instead of in-place mutation for node images: create new ASG/instance-group resource and attach nodes, then drain old nodes. Avoid changing existing instance templates in-place for minimal drift.
- Keep module variables explicit: variable "node_group_suffix" and "replacement_policy" (values: "create_new" / "inplace_rolling"). Do not infer names from timestamps.
- S3 state handling: add explicit state locking timeouts in CI so long plans don't cause deadlocks.
- Provider pinning: lock provider versions in module to avoid surprise provider behavior (aws 4.x vs 5.x differences in attachment ordering).
- TF trick: use lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true } on load-balancer attachment resources and a small pre-check script that asserts backend target registration before destroying old attachment.
- Secrets: never render long-lived credentials in TF outputs; use dynamic references to KMS-wrapped secrets.

Compatibility matrix (quick reference):
- Control plane v3.4.x <-> Runtime v2.9.x: partial feature parity (no streaming headers).
- Control plane v3.5.x <-> Runtime v3.0.x: expected full API compatibility (recommended target).
- If deploying runtime v3.0.x against control-plane v3.4.x: enable compatibility shim (shim-mode=legacy-api) on proxy; expect 1–2 degraded metrics.
- API surface to validate: /health, /v1/generate (headers + streaming), /v1/kvcache/admin.

Phased migration steps (detailed):
0) Change-id: generate a unique id (e.g., MIG-20251102-asha) and tag all artifacts/TF runs.
1) Create TF workspace for the change and run terraform plan in CI with staging varfile. Save plan artifact.
2) Provision shadow node group (create_new policy). Wait for instances to be healthy in monitoring (node exporter, agent alive, GPU visible).
3) Push runtime artifact and sidecar config to shadow nodes (immutable artifact approach). Run: ssh -> sudo systemctl restart runtime.service; check /var/log/runtime/boot.log contains model load success.
4) Warm caches: run scripted preloads for the top-10 model families used by the tenant(s). Track model load time and memory usage.
5) Configure proxy routing rule: route 1% of p95-weighted traffic to shadow pool by header or client-id.
6) Observe for 30m: token latency, error rate, cpu/gpu saturation, kv hit-rate. Have a runbook watch channel with SRE + SE on-call.
7) If metrics stable (no >2x p99, error delta <0.2%), increase to 10% and repeat monitors for 30–60m.
8) If at any stage a threshold breach occurs, immediately flip the traffic back to primary and escalate; keep shadow nodes running for hot-fix deployment.
9) When at 100% and stable for 2 hours, mark migration completed: reconcile TF state to promote new group as primary name (if using blue/green naming) and destroy old group after final drain.

Rollback and emergency backout (explicit steps):
- Rollback trigger conditions: >1% absolute increase in error rate for 5m, sustained p99 >2x baseline for 10m, or model degradation incidents reported by CS.
- Immediate action: update routing rule to 0% for shadow pool (api call to routing service) and confirm client-side retries are hitting primary.
- If TF plan has already removed resources, recover by re-applying previous plan with --target to recreate old attachments, or restore from plan-generated state snapshot. Keep a "golden-plan" artifact for quick re-apply.
- For stateful control-plane changes: revert DB migrations using idempotent down scripts (pre-registered in change set) and restore snapshot if necessary.
- Post-rollback: collect debug bundle (systemd logs, runtime metrics, kernel ring buffer, gpu stats) and attach to JIRA ticket.

Validation and smoke tests (examples):
- Health check: curl -f -sS -H "X-Change-Id: MIG-20251102-asha" https://runtime.private.cluster.local/health || exit 1
- Generate sanity: curl -X POST https://runtime.../v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"say hi","max_tokens":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer X' | jq '.status=="ok"'
- Cache verification: run kvcache admin query to assert prefix hit-rate > 90% after warm-up.

Observability playbook:
- Create temporary dashboards scoped to change-id tag so alerts and metrics are isolated.
- Add a log-level bump on sidecars to DEBUG for the canary window only, and rotate back after.
- Ensure trace sampling for canary traffic at 100% to capture rare errors.

Operational knobs and safety defaults to set pre-migration:
- Default routing weight cap per change: 20% per hour by policy (prevents accidental rapid ramp).
- Automatic fallback timer: if canary not at 100% within 6 hours, trigger automated rollback check and page SRE.
- Quarantine: nodes reporting GPU ECC errors or kernel oops move to quarantine ASG via lambda and do not receive traffic.

Open questions / action items:
- A1: Validate whether older on-prem customers have devices behind NAT with MTU smaller than 1500; need explicit MTU test script (assigned to Diego).
- A2: We should incorporate a post-migration TTL-based cache invalidation strategy for KV entries to prevent stale-model outputs (Priya to prototype).
- A3: Decide whether control-plane v3.5 rollout requires two-step DB migration (backfill + cutover) or in-place online migration (SRE to review).
- A4: Determine support window for legacy API shim: how long will we accept shim-mode in production? (product + eng to agree).

Postmortem skeleton (to be filled if incident occurs):
- Timeline, change-id, actors, decision points, root cause, corrective actions, preventive measures, and rolling retrospective meeting notes.

Appendix: quick TF snippets and commands (examples):
- Create new node group resource pattern:
  resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "runtime_new" {
    name = "runtime-${var.node_group_suffix}-new"
    lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }
    // other args
  }
- Simple plan restore step:
  # restore previous known-good state from plan artifact
  terraform workspace select mig-2025
  terraform apply -auto-approve "golden-plan.tfplan"

- Inline health check script (sample):
  #!/bin/bash -e
  set -o pipefail
  curl -fsS -H "X-Change-Id: $1" $2/health || { echo "health-fail"; exit 2; }

Notes and heuristics learned from prior runs:
- Warm caches with representative prompts: short, medium, long contexts to ensure kv eviction patterns are exercised.
- Avoid simultaneous driver/kernel updates with runtime swap — do in dedicated maintenance window.
- Prefer create_before_destroy when changing LB attachments; in-place mutation of LBs has been the root cause of 3 prior incidents (see JIRA-PROJ-900).

Contact and escalation list:
- On-call SRE: sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Eng private deployments: eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai
- Owner for this migration: Asha Patel (asha@redwood.ai)

If you are reviewing this doc: please add comments inline, append missing TF variables you use, and flag any environmental quirks (air-gap, MTU, custom kmod) so we can centralize as preflight checks.

End of notes.
